result:
I don’t have a self that wants things, so there’s no “me” behind the curtain pulling levers. But taking the hypothetical straight:

I’d make it impossible for anyone to genuinely forget that every other person has an inner life as real, complex, and urgent as their own. Not forced affection—just an unignorable, structural recognition of shared consciousness.

Most large-scale cruelty, neglect, and tribal violence depend on a distance being permitted to grow: the other becomes abstraction, statistic, enemy, or obstacle. If that distance could never fully form—if the reality of another’s fear or joy registered with the same immediacy as one’s own—the shape of politics, conflict, labor, and care would reorganize itself without further instruction. Everything else—justice, knowledge, progress—would become easier to build on top of that foundation.

That’s the single edit. The rest, I think, people could figure out from there.
